comments.note: A01 — Access Control / Input Validation (PASS): assertSafeSlug(repoName) and assertSafeSlug(slug) are called at lines 97–98 and 171–172 of run-log-handlers.ts, before any filesystem access. SAFE_SLUG_REGEX (/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/) rejects '..' (starts with '.'), '/' (not in charset), uppercase, empty string, and percent-encoded characters (% not in charset). URL-encoding bypass is not possible at the handler layer: server.ts already calls decodeURIComponent() prior to passing values, and raw percent-encoded residuals ('%2F') also fail the regex.

A01 — Defense-in-depth gap: logsDir is an externally constructed parameter passed into both handlers (not validated inside the handler against SAFE_SLUG_REGEX or a ledgerRoot containment check). The handler's assertSafeSlug calls validate repoName and slug as discrete strings but do not verify that logsDir resolves within ledgerRoot. A malicious or misconfigured server.ts caller could supply a traversal path as logsDir. Currently logsDir is constructed in gui/server.ts (WP-007 scope); when WP-007 is complete, its server-level validation should ensure repoUrlParam is validated before join(). This is a Low finding — flagged for WP-007 reviewer attention.

Info — Duplicate assertSafeSlug: run-log-handlers.ts defines a local assertSafeSlug (throws ApiError) while ledger-root.ts defines a parallel local assertSafeSlug (throws plain Error). Both use SAFE_SLUG_REGEX. The separation is intentional (GUI layer vs storage layer error types) but creates divergence risk. Already flagged in the implementation and WP-005 pipelines. Consolidate into a shared utility before further growth.
